Well, let me think about this year the same way I think about it every year.

I've been on this land thirty years. Eight mu isn't much, but with wheat and maize back-to-back it keeps us fed and puts some cash in hand. My two sons work in town now, so it's mostly me in the fields — my daughter-in-law helps when the wheat comes in, and during maize planting we all pitch in because there's no time to waste.

**On the wheat** — I'll plant around mid-October, right after we get the maize off. I use the same seed variety I've been using, the one everyone in the village plants. I save a little seed from last year's harvest but I usually buy some fresh too, maybe 15 jin per mu. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — two bags of 15-15-15 for every mu, that's what my neighbor does and what I've always done. After the spring green-up when the wheat starts growing again, I put down urea, maybe half a bag per mu. If the wheat looks yellow I put a bit more, if it looks good I save the money. I water it before winter, once in spring at green-up, again at jointing, and one more time when the grain is filling — that's four waterings, the well costs money so I don't water more than I need. I'll spray once for weeds in spring and once for aphids if I see them. A good year I get maybe 400 jin per mu, bad year 350.

**On the maize** — the window is so tight, barely a few days between wheat harvest and maize planting. I hire the man with the no-till planter, he does the whole village. Hybrid seed, the one the seed shop sells most — costs me about 50 yuan a mu. I put down compound fertilizer with the planter, then when the maize is about waist-high at the big trumpet stage I topdress urea, maybe half a bag per mu. If it rains enough I don't need to irrigate, but if June and July are dry I'll water once or twice. I spray herbicide early and watch for the corn borer. Usually get around 450-500 jin per mu.

Money's tight this year like every year, so I buy what I need and no more. If I had more cash I might put on a bit more fertilizer, but I've farmed this way a long time and it works.
